survey: A gold five-pointed sheriff's star badge, seen from the front and tilted slightly clockwise, floating on a purple sunburst background. Each point is bevelled, with a raised rim running around the outline. A solid gold ball sits on each of the five tips and joins the point cleanly. In the centre is a round raised bezel holding a domed red stone. The back and pin are not shown, which is fine for a front view. It is a single solid piece, so it needs no other supports.

errors.where: Star outline: the right point and the bottom point
errors.what: The star is not regular. The angle between the bottom point and the right point is clearly narrower (about 50°) than the angle between the right point and the top point (about 85°). The bottom-left point is also shorter than the others. A tilted view does not explain the difference, so the five points look unevenly spaced.
A domed red jewel sits in a bezel at the centre. Real sheriff's stars have a flat engraved centre or a stamped seal, not a gemstone. This is an invented part.

fix: A symmetrical gold sheriff's star badge with five points of equal length, evenly spaced 72° apart, each tipped with an identical gold ball. The centre is a flat round gold disc with a simple engraved ring or a small stamped emblem instead of a gem.
